text:
We should know before the ballot what changes are already being discussed in each sector and what protections we’ll have if they go ahead. We’re being asked to make a decision now, with too much of the detail left until later. That’s why I’m voting No.
#SpeirGorm

author: annmarietg.bsky.social
text:
The deal rules out industrial action on matters it covers. So before voting, I want to know which changes require union agreement. If management wants to change our hours, move staff between sites or change who can compete for promotion, what say will we actually have?
#SpeirGorm

author: annmarietg.bsky.social
text:
3/5 Unions are to be consulted before substantial changes. If there’s still a disagreement, it goes through the dispute process. In the meantime, staff are expected to cooperate with what the agreement calls “normal ongoing change”. Who decides what counts as normal?
#SpeirGorm

author: annmarietg.bsky.social
text:
The draft opens the door to reviews of recruitment and promotion, changes to hours and rosters, and redeployment. Blended working stays under review. It also backs changes to how we work as AI and automation are rolled out. The detailed sector plans are due by 1 March 2027.

#SpeirGorm

author: annmarietg.bsky.social
text:
We’re being asked to commit to industrial peace through March 2029 before we see the detailed plans for changes in our workplaces. That’s a big commitment to make with so much still to be worked out.

#SpeirGorm
